esco_description: Financial auditors collect and examine financial data for clients, organisations and companies. They ensure the financial data is properly maintained and free of material misstatements due to error or fraud, that it adds up, and functions legally and effectively. They review lending and credit policies or numbers in databases and documents, evaluate, consult and assist the source of the transaction if necessary. They use their review of the client's financial governance as assurance to give testimony to the shareholders, stakeholders and board of directors of the organisation or company that all is up to par.

pad_quotes: II. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: "Funding of technical, E&S, pre-feasibility, feasibility studies and climate risk analysis for the preparation of selected RE projects.", III. PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION: "The PUC will be  in-charge  of:  (i)  supporting  project  planning  (implementation  of  work-plans,  budget  estimates,  M&E implementation plans, and so on); (ii) actively overseeing project implementation to ensure quality and timely progress; (iii) implementing the M&E arrangements for the project, including its reporting requirements; (iv) ensuring compliance with agreed procurement, disbursements, and financial management (FM) policies and procedures; (v) supervising the implementation and compliance with the Environmental and Social requirements; and (vi) ensuring regular reports on the progress of the project to monitoring and evaluation.", IV. PROJECT APPRAISAL SUMMARY: "The rationale for this risk rating builds on the following aspects: (i) the physical interventions planned under the project are small-scale, located in brownfield areas and are not expected to cause significant adverse risks and impacts on areas of high value or sensitivity or human populations, (ii) the environmental and social (E&S) risks and impacts potentially generated by the planned physical investments are expected to range from low to moderate primarily site-specific (focusing on the areas interfered with by civil works), temporary, reversible and manageable through readily available and cost-effective mitigation measures; anticipated downstream implications of the planned TA activities are also expected to range from low to moderate and be manageable through ToR consistent with the ESF; (iii) PUC and MACCE have no experience or limited experience implementing Bank-financed projects but have relevant in-house ESRM capacity and are committed to reinforcing their E&S team from an early stage of the project to ensure implementation in a manner consistent with ESF requirements, and (iv) the absence of relevant contextual factors that can exacerbate the project's E&S risks and impacts."

PROJECT APPRAISAL SUMMARY: "The rationale for this risk rating builds on the following aspects: (i) the physical interventions planned under the project are small-scale, located in brownfield areas and are not expected to cause significant adverse risks and impacts on areas of high value or sensitivity or human populations, (ii) the environmental and social (E&S) risks and impacts potentially generated by the planned physical investments are expected to range from low to moderate primarily site-specific (focusing on the areas interfered with by civil works), temporary, reversible and manageable through readily available and cost-effective mitigation measures; anticipated downstream implications of the planned TA activities are also expected to range from low to moderate and be manageable through ToR consistent with the ESF; (iii) PUC and MACCE have no experience or limited experience implementing Bank-financed projects but have relevant in-house ESRM capacity and are committed to reinforcing their E&S team from an early stage of the project to ensure implementation in a manner consistent with ESF requirements, and (iv) the absence of relevant contextual factors that can exacerbate the project's E&S risks and impacts."

pad_quotes: II. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: "Funding of technical, E&S, pre-feasibility, feasibility studies and climate risk analysis for the preparation of selected RE projects.", III. PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION: "The PUC will be  in-charge  of:  (i)  supporting  project  planning  (implementation  of  work-plans,  budget  estimates,  M&E implementation plans, and so on); (ii) actively overseeing project implementation to ensure quality and timely progress; (iii) implementing the M&E arrangements for the project, including its reporting requirements; (iv) ensuring compliance with agreed procurement, disbursements, and financial management (FM) policies and procedures; (v) supervising the implementation and compliance with the Environmental and Social requirements; and (vi) ensuring regular reports on the progress of the project to monitoring and evaluation.", IV. PROJECT APPRAISAL SUMMARY: "The rationale for this risk rating builds on the following aspects: (i) the physical interventions planned under the project are small-scale, located in brownfield areas and are not expected to cause significant adverse risks and impacts on areas of high value or sensitivity or human populations, (ii) the environmental and social (E&S) risks and impacts potentially generated by the planned physical investments are expected to range from low to moderate primarily site-specific (focusing on the areas interfered with by civil works), temporary, reversible and manageable through readily available and cost-effective mitigation measures; anticipated downstream implications of the planned TA activities are also expected to range from low to moderate and be manageable through ToR consistent with the ESF; (iii) PUC and MACCE have no experience or limited experience implementing Bank-financed projects but have relevant in-house ESRM capacity and are committed to reinforcing their E&S team from an early stage of the project to ensure implementation in a manner consistent with ESF requirements, and (iv) the absence of relevant contextual factors that can exacerbate the project's E&S risks and impacts."

They also consult their clients on their causes and policies.
